task.title: Keep a checkout packed so synchronizing commands stay fast
task.description:
Workbook stores each task and each relic as a private Git ref whose tip is a commit. A relic is a record beside tasks that holds specs, plans, decisions and similar material.

This is a follow-up from the relic benchmarks (story 5). It was left out of the first six relics stories on purpose.

## Problem

Git reads every ref a checkout holds, and the commit at its tip, when it fetches and when it pushes. A commit stored as a loose file costs more to read than one in a pack. So a command that synchronizes gets slower as a checkout gathers loose commits, for tasks and relics alike.

Git normally packs a checkout by itself, but Workbook passes `--no-auto-maintenance` on every fetch. A checkout that only Workbook writes to is therefore never packed until the person runs another Git command that triggers maintenance, or `git gc`.

Measured by hand on 2026-11-26 in a scratch project (Apple M5 Pro, Git 2.54.0, 15 runs each), `workbook update` with automatic synchronization took:

- 559 ms with no relics;
- 714 ms with 1,000 relics whose commits were loose files;
- 553 ms after one `git repack -a -d` of that checkout.

`docs/architecture.md`, "Relic benchmarks", records this and says no change is decided.

## Wanted

Decide how Workbook keeps this cost down, then build it. Options seen so far:

1. Let Workbook's fetch run Git's automatic maintenance, or run `git maintenance run --auto` after a command that wrote. Find out first why `--no-auto-maintenance` was added, since it may guard against a slow or racing `gc` in the middle of a command.
2. Hide relic refs from the connectivity check of a task command's fetch with `fetch.hideRefs`. This helps the fetch only; the push still reads every ref.
3. Do nothing in Workbook, and have `workbook doctor` or the docs tell the person to run `git gc`.

## Done when

- The choice and its tradeoff are recorded in `docs/architecture.md`.
- The relic benchmark has a scenario that measures a synchronizing task command in a checkout written to since its last pack, with and without relics, and reports it.
- With the chosen change, that scenario with 1,000 relics is within 10 % of the same scenario with none.
- No command packs or prunes in a way that can lose an object another running Workbook command just wrote.

## Not in this story

Packing at the tasks remote. A self-hosted remote's loose refs are documented already.
